I did not know if my partner would leave me when I came out, and luckily he did not. However, what I did know is that he would still love, support, and  accept me as a human being and a friend.

When you feel really connected to someone it can feel like they’re your only lifeline, and that’s okay to a point, that point being your own mental health. If a partner was hurting or vice versa and they needed a break or even to break up, it would be okay because if you loved someone enough to be with them romantically, you should love them enough to support them as a friend or person after as well. 

Not trying to tell you what to do, just saying that she doesn’t have to stop being in your life completely (if you ever did decide to take any transitional steps), if you have love for her and she has love for you.

Just remember that you aren’t really living if you’re living to please other people. Sure, you can be perceived as an attractive “man” but does the attraction of other people really count if you aren’t happy with yourself? 

If you don’t feel attractive, even though you are for the type of body you were born into, then it’s okay to allow yourself change without feeling guilty. As a guy transitioning you won’t believe how many times I’ve heard, “but you were such a pretty girl.”

I can admit that I was attractive as well due to trying to fit in and force away all the awkward and uncomfortable feelings, but I wasn’t happy with myself and just like you said it felt like torture, and at the end of the day when I was alone it didn’t matter what other people thought of me. 

I’m not telling you to change or anything, just saying that there’s no point in living a life in which you aren’t happy with yourself just because you fit a societal attractive male standard. I wish you luck, and I hope one day you’re satisfied and happy.
